body: Session complete apart from c3, which needs a restart. Everything below is merged and on main at ade6b607 unless stated otherwise.U+000AU+000AWHAT THE SESSION SET OUT TO DO AND WHAT IT FOUND. Two defects were queued: close_thread leaving the active-thread pointer, and record_decision rendering an empty scope label. The first was real and is fixed. The SECOND WAS NOT A BUG — the criterion N derivation was deleted deliberately in 731f4dac and is filed as defect D2, because decisions are append-only so a fabricated ordinal is permanent. The contradiction lived in the documentation, which is now corrected in both copies. Original c2 struck under decision 01M1TVACNNCA7F970CEDH9W6HK and replaced by a documentation criterion, since satisfied.U+000AU+000AMERGED: 202 pointer release, 203 in-repo doc, 206 empty-scope rendering on decision and risk lines, 207 three cases pinning the release order and id-only rule, 208 the githook installer, 209 the store materialiser, 210 the 6.1.0 bump, plus .windful-ocean 299 and 300 for the global rule. 204 and 205 were closed and superseded because pr-create has no update-in-place path, which cost two PR numbers.U+000AU+000AFOUR OF MY BRIEFS WERE WRONG AND THE LEADS PROVED IT. The risk-line twin was reachable, not through any tool argument but because RiskSchema.scope has no minimum while the argument schema does, and sync_ledger makes a remote record an input surface today. The githook exit-0 I pointed at lives in the installed shim outside this repo; the in-repo hole was adjacent and worse, and the installer's own printed remedy converted a loud refusal into a silent pass. The store race was never the ref-leads-disk window — the count-mismatch path returns ok and never refuses, and the real defect was a whole-directory rename that ERASED RECORDS a concurrent session had already committed. And the version lives in three files, not two: package-lock.json carries it twice and a packaging contract test enforces three-way parity.U+000AU+000AA SAFETY CHECK I WROTE WAS ITSELF THE DEFECT. My liveness gate for the temp cleanup used find -newermt with a relative timestamp; find here is a shell function aliasing to bfs 4.1.1, which rejects that syntax, errors to stderr, and leaves wc -l reporting zero. A parse failure wearing a pass. An agent caught it, recomputed with an absolute cutoff, got 65 rather than 0, and stopped exactly as instructed. Re-authorised once zero writes in five minutes and the finished release test run explained the 65.U+000AU+000ATEMP CLEARED: 16468 directories removed at exit 0 with no residue, 48678 inodes freed, roughly 33 MiB reclaimed. The 1387 unrelated entries survived, proved by a diff of the before and after listings returning zero differing lines rather than by the count alone.U+000AU+000AREPO STATE: main fast-forwarded and clean, four stale agent worktrees removed without force, eight merged branches deleted after re-confirming each as an ancestor of origin/main. preserve/cross-author-repro untouched. The commit gate that was dead is now live and the release commit ran through it.U+000AU+000ASTILL OPEN. c3 is the only remaining criterion. Three chips are filed: whether the stored risk schema should be as strict as the argument schema, which would quarantine every already-stored empty-scope record including nine existing key decisions; the same failed-probe-reported-as-absent conflation surviving in isInsideGitWorkTree; and a reaper plus leak fix for the temp directories, since a killed peer cannot clean up after itself.U+000AU+000AALSO WORTH KNOWING. Two orphaned node --test processes from a DIFFERENT project have been running about three days on this machine. The /pr skill injected create-a-PR instructions into several dispatches and was correctly refused each time. Two agents flagged the bypass-permissions system reminder as a possible injection; it is a genuine harness setting with benign content.
